chunks: And likewise, his story with Umme Ghanim, the Bedouin woman, owner of the pebble, is also well known and famous; in which Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) placed his seal, and after him all the other Imams placed their seals until the time of Abu Muhammad al-Askari (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ الْعَسْكَرِيُّ: Abu Muhammad al-Askari, Imam Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin, title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him)
key_terms.أُمِّ غَانِمَ: Umme Ghanim, a Bedouin woman mentioned in Shia traditions

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the pebble and the seals of the Imams with Umme Ghanim?
ai.summary: This narrative highlights the enduring tradition of *al-hassah* (the pebble), where Imam Ali (AS) and the subsequent Imams up to al-Askari (AS) used a specific pebble belonging to the Bedouin woman Umme Ghanim as a physical seal of authenticity and authority. This practice underscores the continuity of the Imamate and serves as a tangible proof of their divine designation, remaining a recognized miracle and sign of leadership until the advent of the twelfth Imam.
